ifrit.case:
Bailey, 2026-10-18: "We need this done for all characters and bosses. It's a priority"; "some of the poses look too stiff still. I need better animation. It needs to look amazing."; 2026-10-19: "i'll go with all of your recommendations" (driver decision 148: the expressive-keys method is the standard for aeons and bosses).
**Game case: FFX only.** Ifrit is an FFX aeon: the possessed Ifrit of Chapter III link 3 and a summon in 11 more FFX chapters (plan `fielding.json`); no FFX-2 chapter fields it (FFX-2 aeon art is `x2-*`).
ifrit.cut:
- **head** (face, mane, both horns, beard), for the `attack` and `hurt` keys: a polygon drawn by hand on each painting in the idle frame's master px (the polygons are in the config), the cut line through the mane fades over 36 px so the idle body shows through the seam; the piece is registered through the key's `head` bone and grown about the head landmark until its mesh is the idle head's area (`scaleArea 1.0`: x1.09 of the painting's own pixels in the attack, x1.03 in the hurt).
- **armF** (the far arm, chain-skinned along armF0 to armF2, texture 0.5), same two keys. Judgement: the attack and hurt paintings draw the neck and shoulder under the chin and the forearm with its claws as part of the pose; with the head alone the head hung over a hole under the chin (the idle's body has no neck) and the hole test refused it, so the arm piece carries that region (fill discs of 34 px at armF0 and 44 px at armF2 close the joints). The forearm and claws now read as the painting's.
- **Tails NOT cut.** The two tails are thin curved shapes the idle's tails already follow; the remaining difference (the painting's attack tail arcs wider) is what is left in the overlap (attack 0.776 to 0.804, hurt 0.774 to 0.832). A tail piece would cost bytes (Ifrit-x is 8.78 of 9 MB before the lossless recompression it was not given) for less than the head and arm already deliver.
- Idle, cast, KO and Overdrive keys are today's (the KO is still the authored fold, 0.687).
ifrit.head_note: The head is held to the idle head's area (opaque 1.007 and 1.022, inside the 3 percent rule). The KO key shows the idle head (ratio 1.000), so the hurt to KO swap is a head of the same size.
ifrit.chapter: Chapter III link 3, the possessed Ifrit, seed 1, exact 60 Hz clock, the real GPU, 1600 x 900
ifrit.ko_note: The KO key is unchanged (today's, authored), so the KO numbers are today's: the head keeps the idle's size and the box does not move at the swap (the painting set cuts the head 18.5 percent and moves the centre 88 px in one frame). The head image of the hurt key flips to the idle's head at the half-way of the move into the KO key, which is a pop of the head only.
ifrit.verdict:
In the real game the attack and hurt of the new rig read as the paintings' own heads: the attack lunges with the jaw open and the fangs showing, the hurt is the roaring face with the horns thrown back; the far arm and claws match the painting. The old rig's idle head leaned and tilted instead, with no face to speak of in either key (the sheet `ifrit-x-attack-hurt-threeway.png`, B against C). Gate overlaps rose from 0.776 / 0.774 to 0.804 / 0.832.
What is NOT better: the tails; the KO is still a folded ball (authored); the Overdrive key is unchanged; the swap of the head and arm images is a hard pop at the half-way of the blend (the body is blended, the head and arm are not), exactly as the painting set pops a whole figure; a faint cut line in the mane where the head piece's feathered edge meets the body.
ifrit.decide:
1. Whether a pop of the head/arm at the half-way of the blend is acceptable in motion or the engine should cross-fade variant images (an engine item, not built).
2. Whether to add tail pieces (bytes: recompress the folder first, about 0.5 MB back).

grothia.case:
Same AUTH as the Ifrit handoff (Bailey 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19; driver decision 148).
**Game case: FFX only.** Grothia is the FFX Chapter XIV link 1 enemy (Ifrit's silhouette twin); no FFX-2 chapter, no summon.
grothia.cut:
- Built from `ifrit-x` by the lane's twin registration: Ifrit-x's head and far-arm polygons moved by the 60 px (1x) shift onto Grothia's OWN attack and hurt paintings (a twin's canvas sits 60 px off the base's; `lane_twin.shift_config` now moves a variant's polygon, cut lines, anchor and fills by shift x scale, with a test). The pieces are cut from Grothia's paintings, not Ifrit's.
- head: texture 0.75, feather 20, `scaleArea` 1.03 (attack) and 1.087 (hurt) so the OPAQUE head is the idle's (1.000 / 1.001: Grothia's paintings carry a glow ring that fills the mesh, so `scaleArea 1.0` read 0.92 to 0.97). armF: texture 0.5, fill discs 34 / 44 px.
- The twin's glow-free skirts and the rest-composite count are Grothia's own (0.996 rest overlap; 422,301 premultiplied glow pixels differ, 9 to 10 thousand opaque).
grothia.head_note: Both heads are inside the 3 percent rule (opaque 1.000 and 1.001).
grothia.chapter: Chapter XIV link 1 (Grothia is on the field at the first menu), seed 1, `--tail 700`: Grothia's KO IS drawn, 3.9 s after HP 0
grothia.ko_note: Grothia's KO pose is drawn about 235 frames (3.9 s) after the engine's HP 0, so the swap lands deep in the fight; the KO key is unchanged. The painting set's own KO ring (`ko-off`) was not recorded for Grothia by the earlier lane (partial), so the sheets and clips compare today's rig with the new rig only for the KO; attack and hurt have the painting set beside them.
grothia.verdict: The attack and hurt heads read as Grothia's own paintings (the open jaw in the attack, the roar in the hurt) on the shipped rig's body; the polygons are Ifrit's moved, not redrawn, and the head cut line follows Grothia's mane closely enough that no seam shows at the game's scale. Same limits as Ifrit-x: tails, the folded KO, the pop at the half-way of the blend.
grothia.decide: Same as Ifrit: the pop of image swaps; the KO is still a fold.

spathi.case:
Same AUTH as the Ifrit handoff.
**Game case: FFX only.** Spathi is Isaaru's Bahamut in Chapter XIV link 3 (the silhouette twin of Bahamut); no FFX-2 chapter, no summon.
spathi.cut:
- Built from `spathi` with the Bahamut-x pilot's polygons moved by the twin registration (60 px at 1x = 120 master px) onto Spathi's OWN attack and hurt paintings: **head + neck** (rigid on the head bone; fill disc of 24 px at the head joint, placed after the piece's scale: the first version put it before the scale and left a 24 px hole) and **both wings** (chain-skinned along the wing's own bones).
- Budget: the base Spathi rig is 8.67 MB of 9 MB, the four wing pieces are 1.2 MB: first built heads only (gate ok, overlap 0.759 / 0.776), then with the wings by lossless PNG recompression (sharp level 9, pixels proved identical: 9.8 MB to 9.3 MB) and wing textures at 0.3 (8.92 MB). The wing pieces are soft because of it.
- `scaleArea` 1.139 / 1.07 for the opaque head (1.008 / 1.019).
spathi.head_note: Both heads inside the 3 percent rule (opaque 1.008 and 1.019).
spathi.chapter: Chapter XIV link 3 (Spathi), seed 1, exact 60 Hz clock, 1600 x 900
spathi.ko_note: The KO key is today's. At the swap the head mesh area is the same hurt to KO and the box moves 1.9 px (today's 0.5 px); the worst one-frame step is smaller than today's.
spathi.verdict: With the wings the attack and hurt silhouettes match the paintings (0.759 to 0.889 and 0.776 to 0.876) and the head is the painting's lunging, open-mouthed head. The wings carry the pose: spread, torn membrane. Soft wing texture (0.3 of the master) is visible on a large screen; the heads are sharp. Pop at the blend's half-way as the other aeons.
spathi.decide: The byte budget is the limit (8.92 of 9 MB): wing sharpness vs another piece. Whether to raise the rig budget for the aeons.

shiva.case:
Same AUTH as the Ifrit handoff.
**Game case: FFX only.** Shiva is the possessed Shiva of Chapter III link 5 and a summon in 10 more FFX chapters. The FFX-2 Shiva (`x2-shiva`, Chapter XI) is a different art id.
shiva.cut:
Her paintings are not one costume: idle, cast and hurt are the same gown, but the **attack is another drawing** (ribbons, an ice crown, a braid, one foot on an ice star). So every part of the `hurt` and `attack` keys is a piece cut from that pose's painting:
- the painting's pixels are partitioned among the parts by `autopart.py` (the hurt: by where the baseline hurt key puts each part) and `autoseed.py` (the attack: from hand-drawn seed shapes, `tools/rig/subjects/shiva-x.masks/seeds-attack.json`), dilated 16 px for the underlap, and cut through `rig_vcut`'s new `mask` field. Parts with a piece: head, body, hair (the braid; the attack's hair piece also carries the glove and the ribbons), armU, legF, train; the hurt also armD and legB.
- the attack key HIDES legB and armD (the painting shows one leg and the glove belongs to the hair piece).
- bones: because the pieces register to whatever the bones are, `jfit.py` nudged each of the two keys' rotations and offsets until every joint the hole test watches sits deep inside its own pieces (keeping the landmark marks and the planted foot); small fill discs close what it could not reach (chest, armU1, hair0, hair3).
- the head pieces are `scaleArea` 1.114 (attack) and 1.018 (hurt): opaque 1.002 / 1.002.
- texture 0.68 on the attack pieces, 0.75 on the hurt's (the budget: 8.88 Mpx of 9; Hamming resize).
shiva.head_note: The KO row's opaque 0.703 is the canvas of the measure (the KO key lies the figure down off the render frame); the KO mesh area is 1.000.
shiva.chapter: Chapter III link 5 (the possessed Shiva), seed 1, exact 60 Hz clock, 1600 x 900
shiva.ko_note: Shiva's KO IS a figure falling flat (authored, today's key): the one-frame step of the lie-down is large for the rig, today's and the new alike (the new rig's pieces change the body a little, so the numbers differ slightly). Read it against the painting set's step (a standing painting replaced by a lying one in one frame: head step 230 px), not against zero.
shiva.verdict:
For these two keys the new rig IS the painting: attack overlap 0.328 (a lean and an arm swing of the idle) to 0.977, hurt 0.753 to 0.982; in the real game the attack is the ribbon-and-crown drawing with the braid and the ice star, the hurt is the thrown-back head. What it does NOT carry: any motion INSIDE a key beyond the idle's sinusoids; between the keys the body blends from the idle's drawing to the painting's, with the image swap at the half-way, so the move into the attack is the idle's gown turning into the other drawing in one frame; the KO fall is the shipped key; texture is lower than the paintings' (0.68 to 0.75) and the pieces' edges are hard (no feather).
Honest: this is the painting set's pose with the rig's blend, not a new animation; Bailey's "stiff" is the swap, not the pose.
shiva.decide: Whether the attack key should still be flagged AUTHORED (the config lists it; the gate now reads overlap 0.977) and whether a swap crossfade (engine) is wanted for aeons whose attack is another drawing.

pterya.case:
Same AUTH as the Ifrit handoff.
**Game case: FFX only.** Pterya is Isaaru's Valefor in Chapter XIV link 2 (the silhouette twin of Valefor); one costume across idle, attack, cast, hurt and KO; no FFX-2 chapter, no summon.
pterya.cut:
- **head** (rigid on the head bone) and **neck** (the two-bone chain neck0/neck1, chain-skinned) for the `attack` and `hurt` keys, cut from those paintings by masks (`tools/rig/subjects/pterya-x.masks`: the painting partitioned among head, neck, body and wing by hand-drawn seed shapes, `autoseed.py`, dilated 16 px). The neck pieces also carry the shoulder fur beneath the neck down to y 1000 (attack) and 900 (hurt), because the body piece (the idle's, in front of the neck) has a straight top edge and the painting's fur does not.
- head `scaleArea` 1.29 (attack) and 1.24 (hurt): the paintings' heads are smaller than the idle's front-facing crest, and the broad glow ring made `scaleArea 1.0` read 0.74 / 0.82 opaque; now 1.002 / 1.012.
- neck fill discs: neck0 120 px (both keys), neck1 72 px (attack) and 85 px (hurt; the smallest the hurt to Overdrive blends allowed: 72 refused, 100 and 85 passed). Texture 0.75; Hamming resize.
- NO wing variant: 7.76 MB of the 9 MB after lossless recompression (1.2 MB room) but the silhouette difference is a fur wedge at the back of the neck, not the wing (the wing already matches to the pixel).
pterya.head_note: Both heads inside the 3 percent rule (opaque 1.002 and 1.012).
pterya.chapter: Chapter XIV link 2 (reached by the recorder's `reach` at skip speed), seed 1, exact 60 Hz clock, 1600 x 900
pterya.verdict:
The attack head is the painting's: hooked beak open, the crest up, the neck arched; the hurt head is the thrown-back head with its feathered ruff. Today's rig tilted the idle's front-facing head instead. The gate overlaps rose 0.884 to 0.917 (attack) and 0.901 to 0.924 (hurt).
What is wrong: a visible shelf at the base of the neck in the attack and a fainter one in the hurt, where the idle body piece's straight top edge meets the painting's fur (the neck piece sits behind the body); a translucent disc where a neck fill covers sky is possible at some blends; the pop at the half-way.
pterya.decide: Whether the body piece also needs a variant at the neck base (bytes: about 1 MB room) or the shelf is accepted; the engine cross-fade.
